news.title: World Cup stadium could be demolished to make way for 80,000-seater new arena
news.lede: A FORMER World Cup stadium could be demolished to make way for a brand new 80,000-seater arena. The Deutsche Bank Park was featured multiple times during the tournament in Germany in 2006. The iconic ground was the setting for England‘s 1-0 victory over Paraguay and four other matches at that edition of the World Cup. It has also been known as the Waldstadion, the Neues Waldstadion and the Commerzbank-Arena.

news.title: Africa’s Moment? The Battle To Host Football’s 2030 World Cup Final
news.lede: Football’s ultimate fixture awaits its scheduling. The first major triumph of the 2030 World Cup will come long before the kick-off of the tournament, to be co-hosted by Morocco, Portugal and Spain. It will be the decision on which of the three countries gets the prestige of hosting the final, a call that world football’s governing body, FIFA, will make. Exactly when is unclear, and each passing month only heightens the tension ahead of the announcement.

news.title: Roman Vega: The surprise inclusion in Argentina’s post-World Cup squad
news.lede: The defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final marked the end of one chapter for Argentina. But as Lionel Scaloni announced his squad for the national team's first three friendlies since that painful night, it became clear that the next chapter would look different. There was continuity, certainly. But there were also absences, suspensions, returning faces and, most intriguingly, a collection of young players knocking loudly on the door.

news.title: Football and Formula 1: Azerbaijan eases visa rules for major sporting events
news.lede: Azerbaijan is using simplified entry procedures to support the arrival of international visitors attending major sporting events. After introducing a special visa arrangement in late August for the Formula 1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the authorities have now adopted a similar measure for the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival, which will be held in the Azerbaijani capital in October. Under a decision published on September 21, 2026, certain foreign nationals and stateless persons traveling to Azerbaijan in connection with the football tournament will be able to obtain their visas upon arrival at the country’s international airports from September 22 through November 5, 2026.
